name: Programming Languages and Frameworks
blurb: The languages AI is written in and the frameworks built on top of them, tracked by adoption, releases, licence, and integrations.

reading.body:
This hub defines the software stack for AI as three layers: programming languages, AI frameworks, and inference engines, but it currently contains no tracked items or metrics.

The three layers cover Python, Rust, C++, Mojo, and Julia for languages; LangChain, LlamaIndex, DSPy, and Semantic Kernel for frameworks; and vLLM, TensorRT, and llama.cpp for inference engines. The stated tracking dimensions are adoption, releases, licence, and integrations, yet the total is zero and no points are listed.

The data therefore describes a taxonomy, not evidence. It does not show which language or framework is most used, nor does it connect any of these tools to compute, buildings, or power.
